narrative:
Your loan was denied because the model estimated a 38.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. That does not mean failure is certain; it means roughly 38 out of 100 applicants with a similar profile would be expected to have repayment difficulty. Although this is below 50%, it was above the bank’s approval cutoff.

The strongest factor was your checking-account status: your account was below zero. Only 12.6% of approved applicants had this status, and this was the main signal pushing the prediction toward bad credit. The second most important factor was your savings information being unknown or none. This actually worked in your favor, pushing toward good credit, even though about one third of approved applicants also show unknown or no savings. The third factor was your stated loan purpose, listed as “other,” which also pushed toward good credit. The checking-account signal was strong enough to outweigh those favorable signals.

Next, ask the bank to confirm the information used, especially your checking balance. Provide statements showing any savings or a corrected account status, and document the loan purpose clearly. Ask what balance, documentation, or risk cutoff you would need to meet before reapplying. Reducing the requested amount or adding a guarantor may also help, but confirm this with the lender first.
